messages:
Amanda L.: Heads-up — opened PR to reconcile wording around 'param' vs 'argument' across guides and examples. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4567. Mostly copy edits but affects a bunch of SDK snippets.
Josh W.: Thanks — is this purely docs text or do any code samples change variable names?
Amanda L.: Docs only. I replaced casual 'arg' with 'parameter' in prose and kept code identifiers intact, except in a few examples where the identifier was literally `arg` — changed those to `param` for clarity.
Priya S.: I can sweep the SDK examples repo and update snippets in the snippet registry. Quick q: do we want to standardize on `parameter` everywhere, or accept `argument` in reference pages?
Sean K.: My take: prefer 'parameter' in user-facing guides and examples because it's consistent with the API reference. Allow 'argument' in deep technical notes if it matches upstream library terminology. Can we add a one-line decision in docs STYLE.md so future PRs follow it?
Amanda L.: Yup — added STYLE.md entry draft in the PR. Short text + two examples. Also found inconsistent phrasing for route names (e.g., 'route' vs 'endpoint') — I left those for a follow-up but called them out in the PR comments.
Priya S.: For SDK snippets: plan is camelCase identifiers in JS/TS examples, snake_case in Python. I'll include a tiny note in each snippet header to make that explicit.
Josh W.: +1. One nit: in the JS snippet you changed `arg` to `param` but the comment still says "pass the arg" — small find-and-replace miss. I'll flag that inline.
Amanda L.: Good catch — fixed. Also adding a tiny code block in the migration guide to show a before/after of example code.
Amanda L.: ```js
// before
client.call({ arg: "value" })
// after
client.call({ param: "value" })
```
Sean K.: That helps. Can we also add a glossary entry: parameter (user-facing name) vs argument (function-level term)? If you add it I'll link from the migration guide.
Amanda L.: Added a short glossary note and linked it.
docs-bot: PR #4567 opened by @Amanda L. — checklist: docs review, snippet sweep, glossary update, link-check.
Priya S.: I'll start the snippet sweep now and post a follow-up thread with any API example diffs. Expect a few small commits.
Josh W.: I'll review the PR tonight. If no major flags, let's merge and then run the staging link-checker so we can catch any broken internal anchors. :thumbsup:
Amanda L.: Thanks everyone — aim to merge by EOD if reviews come in. If we find more route/endpoint friction, I'll spin up a separate thread for that decision so this one stays focused.
